accepted.question: Describe six techniques by which malware infects systems or propagates itself, including how it hides its activity and how it spreads through user interaction.

marking_points.point: Boot sector infection works by replacing the original master boot record with an infected version so the system bootstraps using the malicious MBR.
marking_points.quote: Overwrite the MBR with an infected one
marking_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states overwriting the MBR with an infected version, matching the marking point's boot sector infection mechanism.

marking_points.point: COM executable infection appends the virus body to a program and replaces the program entry point with a jump to the virus body.
marking_points.quote: Replace a program entry point with a jump to a virus body

marking_points.point: EXE executable infection overwrites a program header to switch the entry point to the virus.
marking_points.quote: Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: Rootkits conceal malicious processes and software in the infected system to keep privileged remote access for the author.
marking_points.quote: Rootkits are a type of malware that mask malicious processes and software in the infected systems to ensure privileged remote access.

marking_points.point: Spyware propagates harm by spying on users, stealing logins and passwords and logging keystrokes.
marking_points.quote: spyware are programs that spy on the users. They steal user logins and passwords, document sites visited, log keystrokes and even redirect browsers to unwanted sites.

questions.question: State six facts about substitution ciphers as presented in the lecture, covering how plain-text is transformed, what serves as the key, the security principle involved, and how the Vigenere cipher differs from simple substitution.

marking_points.point: Plain-text letters are swapped for other letters to produce the cipher-text.
marking_points.quote: In substitution ciphers, we replace the plain-text letters with other letters

questions.question: Explain how a rail fence transposition cipher encrypts and decrypts a message.

marking_points.point: Encryption writes the plaintext in a zigzag across rows and reads letters row by row to form the ciphertext.
marking_points.quote: The plain-text is written in a zigzag pattern in rows and form the cipher-text by reading off the letters from the rows.

marking_points.point: Decryption rebuilds the empty rail fence table from the known key, fills rows with ciphertext, then reads in zigzag to recover plaintext.
marking_points.quote: To decrypt a rail fence cipher,  we have to recreate the ‘empty’ rail fence table (as in (A)) using the known key.

questions.question: Describe six (6) aspects of Windows security mechanisms, covering their purpose, the entities they manage, and the risks arising from their complexity.

marking_points.point: Windows provides elaborate built-in facilities for managing user accounts and objects and for controlling access.
marking_points.quote: Windows systems contain complex security mechanisms for user account and object management as well as access control.

marking_points.point: Discretionary access control in Windows permits detailed, fine-grained control over access to diverse entities both within the OS and in applications.
marking_points.quote: DACS enable ﬁne-grained access control of heterogeneous entities in Windows itself as well as applications.

marking_points.point: The very complexity of these mechanisms creates danger, since incorrect configuration or coding defects can cause serious security breaches.
marking_points.quote: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms is also its enemy: misconﬁguration as well as implementation bugs may lead to severe security incidents.

marking_points.point: Processes and threads act as the active subjects on which Windows enforces its security.
marking_points.quote: Windows subjects are processes and threads.

marking_points.point: A subject's security credentials are held in a token that maps the principal to the subject and can carry extra security attributes.
marking_points.quote: Security credentials for a subject are stored in a token.

marking_points.point: Windows 2000 introduced Active Directory, an LDAP-like directory service that organizes users, groups, credentials, resources and security policies.
marking_points.quote: Active directory introduced in Windows 2000 is an LDAP-like directory service for organization of system resources:

questions.question: Describe six techniques by which malware infects systems or propagates itself, including how it hides its activity and how it spreads through user interaction.

marking_points.point: Boot sector infection works by replacing the original master boot record with an infected version so the system bootstraps using the malicious MBR.
marking_points.quote: Overwrite the MBR with an infected one

marking_points.point: COM executable infection appends the virus body to a program and replaces the program entry point with a jump to the virus body.
marking_points.quote: Replace a program entry point                                   with a jump to a virus body

marking_points.point: EXE executable infection overwrites a program header to switch the entry point to the virus.
marking_points.quote: Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: Rootkits conceal malicious processes and software in the infected system to keep privileged remote access for the author.
marking_points.quote: Rootkits are a type of malware that mask malicious processes and software in the infected systems to ensure privileged remote access.

marking_points.point: Spyware propagates harm by spying on users, stealing logins and passwords and logging keystrokes.
marking_points.quote: spyware are programs that spy on the users. They steal user logins and passwords, document sites visited, log keystrokes and even redirect browsers to unwanted sites.

marking_points.point: Cross-site scripting spreads through user interaction when a victim inadvertently clicks an emailed link or an infected image.
marking_points.quote: Inadvertently click on an emailed link

questions.question: Explain six (6) points about biometric mechanisms and technologies, covering how a biometric is defined, the categories of biometric applications, and the strengths and weaknesses of specific biometric technologies.

marking_points.point: A biometric is defined as a physiological or behavioural characteristic of a human being that can distinguish one person from another.
marking_points.quote: A biometric is a physiological or behavioural characteristic of a human being that can distinguish one person from another

marking_points.point: Biometric applications are grouped into two sectors, namely psychological and behavioural.
marking_points.quote: Biometric applications available today are categorized into 2 sectors

marking_points.point: The psychological category includes iris, fingerprints, hand, retinal and face recognition.
marking_points.quote: Psychological: Iris, Fingerprints, Hand, Retinal and Face recognition

marking_points.point: The behavioural category includes voice, typing pattern and signature.
marking_points.quote: Behavioural: Voice, Typing pattern, Signature

marking_points.point: Iris scanning reads the unique pattern of the iris, needs no touch, and overcomes the issues of retinal scanners.
marking_points.quote: Scans unique pattern of iris

marking_points.point: Fingerprint technology suffers from disadvantages such as racial issues, dirt, grime and wounds, finger placement, an oversized database, and spoofing that makes liveness important.
marking_points.quote: Can be spoofed – liveness                                              important!
